description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of tasks across various linguistic families, with the vertical axis listing the categories in descending order of task count, including IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque. The bars are sorted in descending order of task count, with no visual emphasis on any particular bar. The chart provides a clear representation of the distribution of tasks across the different linguistic families.

The vertical axis lists the categories, including IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque, arranged in descending order of task count. The horizontal axis is labeled '# tasks,' ranging from 0 to 80, with tick marks at intervals of 10. IE-Slavic exhibits the highest number of tasks, approximately 80, followed by IE-Romance at around 60 tasks. IE-Germanic and Uralic show similar task counts, both exceeding 40 tasks. Notably, IE-Baltic demonstrates a sharp decline compared to Uralic, with fewer than 15 tasks. Basque, the smallest category, has fewer than 10 tasks, showing a consistent trend of minimal representation across studies. The chart highlights a steady decrease in task counts from IE-Slavic to IE-Baltic, with a more gradual decline observed among the remaining categories.
